ontology.purpose: Build a foundational operations-doctrine ontology from ADRP 3-0 that captures the Army's operational concept (unified land operations) and the conceptual vocabulary used to describe any military operation. The ontology must answer, for each doctrinal concept, what it is defined as, what its components or elements are, what purpose it serves, which higher concept it belongs to, and how it relates to other concepts (e.g., which elements make up combat power, which variables describe an operational environment, which tenets characterize unified land operations). It underpins consistent term usage across other doctrine-derived ontologies.
ontology.scope: IN SCOPE: the nature of military operations and the operational environment (operational and mission variables); the range of military operations and levels of warfare; operational art — its elements (end state, center of gravity, decisive points, lines of operations/effort, tempo, phasing, culmination, operational reach, risk), defeat and stability mechanisms; the Army's operational concept — unified land operations, decisive action and its tasks (offense, defense, stability, defense support of civil authorities), tenets, mission command philosophy; the operations structure — operations process, warfighting functions, operational framework (deep/close/support areas, decisive/shaping/sustaining, main and supporting efforts); combat power and its elements; all definitions and lists the document states. OUT OF SCOPE: detailed tactics, procedures, unit organization, and material found only in subordinate publications.
